title: Beylik of Dulkadir
capsule: The Beylik of Dulkadir (Turkish: Dulkadirli Beyliği) was an Anatolian Turkoman principality founded in 1337 by Zayn al-Din Qaraja of the Bayat tribe, controlling approximately 70,000 km² around Elbistan in the upper Euphrates region of southeastern Anatolia. Positioned as a contested buffer between the Mamluk Sultanate and the Ottoman Empire, the beylik's beys oscillated in their allegiances across nearly two centuries, with Ala al-Dawla Bozkurt (1480–1515) holding the longest reign and briefly aligning with the Safavids against both Mamluks and Ottomans. Ottoman Sultan Selim I destroyed the beylik at the Battle of Turnadağ in August 1515, killing Ala al-Dawla; the territory was converted into an Ottoman sanjak and formally dissolved under the last bey, Ali, by 1522.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Dulkadir around Maraş and Elbistan is well-established from Ottoman and Mamluk sources, but the exact frontier with neighboring beyliks and Mamluk Syria fluctuated and is imprecisely mapped.
